cl_cath_deaths_mephedrone_confirmed.q: How many deaths linked to mephedrone were confirmed?
cl_cath_deaths_mephedrone_confirmed.short: In 25 of 128 alleged deaths, tests after death found no mephedrone.
cl_cath_deaths_mephedrone_confirmed.but: A positive test does not prove cause. A negative test may miss earlier use.
how: By October 2011, 128 deaths in the UK and nearby islands had been linked to mephedrone; 13 results were still pending.
Of 62 deaths studied, mephedrone was the only substance found in 8. Other drugs were common.
One person died weeks later in hospital and had none found after death. Their earlier test evidence is not given.
The authors say tests and incomplete reporting may also miss deaths. They cannot give a death rate.

freq.what: of the 128 alleged deaths had no mephedrone found after death
freq.note: Editors’ rounded calculation: 25/128≈20 in 100; 13 results pending. Negative does not prove no earlier exposure.

cl_opi_deaths_heroin_alone.q: Are heroin overdose deaths always caused by heroin alone?
cl_opi_deaths_heroin_alone.short: Other drugs are often found. That does not show which caused the death.
cl_opi_deaths_heroin_alone.but: These old records cannot tell how many deaths heroin alone caused.
how: In older studies from the USA, Australia and Europe, morphine was the only drug found in 23 to 48 in 100 deaths labelled heroin overdose. Alcohol was found in 29 to 75 in 100.
Many deaths took hours; other people were often present. These are findings relayed by a review.

In England and Wales in 2000, researchers put at least 23 in 100 reported accidental drug-related deaths in categories beyond direct overdose, under their rules. Methadone was the only drug blamed in 4 in 100 direct overdoses; that does not mean no other drug was found.
Heroin exposure may also be missed when its marker breaks down. Blood levels also depend on the specimen and sampling time.

cl_mdma_deaths_fatal_level.q: What level of MDMA in blood is fatal?
cl_mdma_deaths_fatal_level.short: These studies do not establish a fatal cutoff; the measured levels overlap.
cl_mdma_deaths_fatal_level.but: The groups are small. Hospital plasma differs from blood taken at autopsy.
how: In Sheffield, England (1992–2008), levels in deaths attributed to MDMA overlapped levels in injury deaths. The middle value was about 7 times the injury-group value, but was not a cutoff.
The London paper gave levels for 8 survivors that overlapped the 5 measured fatal cases. Some survivors had been severely ill.
A Finnish table’s 0% concerns poisoning with MDMA as the main finding, not every possible contribution. It records what certifiers decided.
Sampling time and specimen matter. None of these studies gives a healthy ordinary-use comparison.

cl_gen_deaths_excited_delirium.short: The label alone does not establish what caused a death.
cl_gen_deaths_excited_delirium.but: The cases were selected for reports. They cannot give the risk per encounter.
how: The reviews describe extreme agitation, but no validated definition or specific autopsy sign. The label is also used with living people.
In 168 published cases, force was recorded in 94 of 104 deaths. That included sedation and electrical weapons as well as physical restraint.
Only 3 cases explicitly had no force; 28 had missing information. A later review also cites deaths attributed to the label without overt restraint.
Researchers disagree about restraint, drugs and the agitated state. These reports cannot tell how much each caused.
